<script>
  // Restore the saved color scheme preference, or
  // enact the browser preference if "automatic", 
  // without expecting DOM load to have completed.
  //
  // Also restore any saved readingmode and ToC display preferences.
  function initializeReadingPreferences() {
    let saved_theme = localStorage.getItem("ar5iv_theme") || "automatic";
    if (saved_theme === "automatic") {
      if (window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches) {
        saved_theme = "dark";
      }
    }
    if (saved_theme == "dark") {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "dark");
    } else {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "light");
    }

    const tocDisplay = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_toc_display');
    if (tocDisplay) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-toc-display", tocDisplay);
    }
    const readingMode = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_reading_mode');
    if (readingMode) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-reading-mode", readingMode);
    }
  }
  // Run as soon as JS starts, to minimize repainting
  initializeReadingPreferences();
</script>

  /* Reading mode hides the chrome and the empty .arxiv-html-header marker: the pinned JS reads
     the marker's display to know which way to toggle. The marker draws no box. */
  .arxiv-html-header { display: contents; }
  html[data-reading-mode="enabled"] :is(.arxiv-html-site-chrome, .arxiv-html-header, .ds-site-footer) { display: none; }
  /* The paper controls' icons are blocks, so they sit centred (the pinned JS shows the theme
     icon by making its span a block). */
  .arxiv-html-site-chrome .ds-site-header-tools svg { display: block; width: 18px; height: 18px; flex-shrink: 0; fill: currentColor; }
  /* ar5iv dims every image in dark mode and puts it on a white wash, for paper figures;
     arXiv's own render as they are (the logo on the bar, the funder logos on their white
     chips). Important: ar5iv's dark rules are unlayered, as specific as
     :root:not([data-theme]) img:not(.ltx_no_dark_filter). */
  :is(.ds-site-header, .ds-site-footer) img { filter: none !important; }
  .ds-site-header img { background-color: transparent !important; }

  /* Wide (the theme's 1280px): the theme lays the body out as a grid whose full-width top rows
     were the band's and its sticky reader bar's. The band takes the first and scrolls away; the
     header, the paper's bar (no site navigation, the paper's controls), takes the second and
     stays in view, the one sticky bar, with the anchor clearance that requires (DESIGN-POLICIES).
     The controls show their names. */
  @media (min-width: 1280px) {
    html { scroll-padding-top: 80px; }
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome { display: contents; }
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome > #ds-announcement { grid-area: announce; }
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome > .ds-site-header { grid-area: header; position: sticky; top: 0; z-index: 3; }
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome .tool-icon { display: none; }
  }
  /* Narrow: the header scrolls away, and the controls show icons (names kept for screen
     readers; Why HTML? goes). The theme's contents panel is fixed below where its old sticky
     bar was, and hidden only once the reader has closed it, so until then it is an invisible box
     over the header and the paper: it shows only while open, under the chrome, in its place in
     the page. The paper's footer (build logs, reporting instructions) keeps the text's side
     inset; the theme gives it none, so it met the screen edges. */
  @media (max-width: 1279px) {
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome .tool-wide { display: none; }
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome .tool-label { position: absolute; width: 1px; height: 1px; overflow: hidden; clip: rect(0 0 0 0); white-space: nowrap; }
    html:not([data-toc-display="block"]) .ltx_page_navbar { display: none; }
    .ltx_page_navbar { position: absolute; top: auto; }
    .arxiv-html-footer { padding-inline: 1rem; }
  }

<article class="ltx_document ltx_authors_1line" lang="en">
<h1 class="ltx_title ltx_title_document">Code World Model 2.0:
<br class="ltx_break">Towards Infinite Controllable Video Generation</h1>
<div class="ltx_authors">
<span class="ltx_creator ltx_role_author">
<span class="ltx_personname"><span id="id1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Ruoyu Wang<sup id="id1.1" class="ltx_sup"><span id="id1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">1,2,∗</span></sup></span> <span id="id2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Hao Zhong<sup id="id2.1" class="ltx_sup"><span id="id2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">1,3,∗</span></sup></span> <span id="id3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Yanming Yang<sup id="id3.1" class="ltx_sup"><span id="id3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">1,2,∗</span></sup></span> <span id="id4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Jiahao Tian<sup id="id4.1" class="ltx_sup"><span id="id4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">1,2,∗</span></sup></span> <span id="id5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lin Liu<sup id="id5.1" class="ltx_sup"><span id="id5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">1,∗,†</span></sup>
<br class="ltx_break" style="--ltx-break-space:3.0pt;"></span>
<span id="id6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Biao Gong<sup id="id6.1" class="ltx_sup"><span id="id6.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">1</span></sup></span> <span id="id7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Guoshan Lu<sup id="id7.1" class="ltx_sup"><span id="id7.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">1</span></sup></span> <span id="id8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Yiding Tian<sup id="id8.1" class="ltx_sup"><span id="id8.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">1</span></sup></span> <span id="id9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Chunhua Shen<sup id="id9.1" class="ltx_sup"><span id="id9.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">3,‡</span></sup></span> <span id="id10" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Zhenzhong Lan<sup id="id10.1" class="ltx_sup"><span id="id10.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">1,2,‡</span></sup></span> <span id="id11" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Chi Zhang<sup id="id11.1" class="ltx_sup"><span id="id11.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">2,‡</span></sup></span>
</span><span class="ltx_author_notes"><span class="ltx_author_notes_content">
<span class="ltx_contact ltx_role_affiliation"><span class="ltx_contact_name">Affiliation: </span><sup id="id12" class="ltx_sup"><span id="id12.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">1</span></sup>Inclusion AI, Ant Group <sup id="id13" class="ltx_sup"><span id="id13.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">2</span></sup>Westlake University <sup id="id14" class="ltx_sup"><span id="id14.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">3</span></sup>Zhejiang University
<br class="ltx_break" style="--ltx-break-space:2.0pt;"><sup id="id15" class="ltx_sup"><span id="id15.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">∗</span></sup>Equal contribution <sup id="id16" class="ltx_sup"><span id="id16.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">†</span></sup>Project leader <sup id="id17" class="ltx_sup"><span id="id17.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">‡</span></sup>Corresponding author
</span></span></span></span></div>

<div id="abstract1" class="ltx_abstract"><h6 class="ltx_title ltx_title_abstract">Abstract</h6>
    
<p id="abstract1.1" class="ltx_p">Visual proxies decouple explicit world-state simulation from photorealistic video synthesis, offering a controllable interface for both offline clip creation and real-time interactive streaming. Yet a practical renderer must address two challenges. Upstream proxies vary from coarse layouts to fine articulated geometry depending on the interaction, and streaming inference must operate in a few causal steps without accumulating drift across self-generated history. We present <span id="abstract1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Invoker-Render</span>, pairing a bidirectional creation model with a causal four-step streaming model under a shared conditioning interface over structural proxies, an appearance reference, and language. Trained on an aligned <math id="abstract1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sim" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>∼</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sim</annotation></semantics></math>200-hour multi-granularity corpus, Invoker-Render honors fine geometric constraints when supplied while synthesizing plausible local motion under coarse proxies, enabling runtime selection of input detail. To bridge bidirectional creation and real-time streaming without compounding step compression and rollout drift, we introduce <span id="abstract1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Progressive Forcing (ProForcing)</span>. ProForcing first trains a causal predictor and distills it into a four-step renderer using histories derived from training videos. Training then shifts to continuous self-generated rollouts. A pipelined serving stack supports efficient streaming inference. Experiments show versatile control across proxy families, granularities, and camera paths, consistent gains over recent streaming baselines, and stable 30-minute racing rollouts that preserve scene and subject appearance.</p>
  
</div>
<div id="p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent ltx_align_center">
<p id="p1.1" class="ltx_p"><a href="https://www.inclusion-ai.org/CodeWorldModel/" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_href ltx_font_bold">Project Page</a>
  <span id="p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#808080;">•</span>  
<a href="https://github.com/inclusionAI/CodeWorldModel" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_href ltx_font_bold">GitHub</a>
  <span id="p1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#808080;">•</span>  
<a href="https://huggingface.co/inclusionAI/invoker-render-1.0" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_href ltx_font_bold">Hugging Face</a></p>
</div>
<div id="p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<div id="p2.1" class="ltx_logical-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_middle" style="width:345.0pt;">

</div>

</figure>

<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
<section id="S1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">1 </span>Introduction</h2>

<div id="S1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Interactive video world models must synthesize coherent observations as user actions alter the environment <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">2</a>, <a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">52</a>, <a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">70</a>, <a href="#bib.bib20" title="" class="ltx_ref">51</a>]</cite>. Rather than simulating both dynamics and appearance in one network, an emerging paradigm maintains explicit state in an upstream engine and delegates visual synthesis to a generative renderer <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">8</a>, <a href="#bib.bib28" title="" class="ltx_ref">20</a>, <a href="#bib.bib37" title="" class="ltx_ref">56</a>]</cite>. Visual and geometric proxies bridge the two stages by prescribing camera paths, layout, and entity motion while leaving photorealistic appearance to the video model <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib26" title="" class="ltx_ref">27</a>, <a href="#bib.bib42" title="" class="ltx_ref">41</a>, <a href="#bib.bib45" title="" class="ltx_ref">7</a>, <a href="#bib.bib55" title="" class="ltx_ref">26</a>]</cite>. Recent systems pair such structural cues with appearance references for offline authoring and real-time rendering <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib39" title="" class="ltx_ref">12</a>, <a href="#bib.bib29" title="" class="ltx_ref">34</a>, <a href="#bib.bib40" title="" class="ltx_ref">31</a>, <a href="#bib.bib41" title="" class="ltx_ref">19</a>, <a href="#bib.bib31" title="" class="ltx_ref">67</a>]</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">In practice, the structural detail appropriate for conditioning depends on the interaction. Broad navigation often requires only coarse scene geometry and root trajectories, whereas close-range interactions demand articulated poses or finer surface structure. Detailed proxies supply tighter constraints at higher construction and transmission cost, while coarse proxies are lightweight to produce yet leave local geometry and motion under-specified. A capable renderer must interpret both regimes faithfully. For example, a rigid mannequin that tracks a character’s root pose should constrain global position and heading without imposing a frozen limb posture on the generated motion.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">We introduce <span id="S1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Invoker-Render</span>, a proxy-conditioned rendering framework comprising a <span id="S1.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">bidirectional creation model</span> and a <span id="S1.p3.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">causal four-step streaming model</span>. Both accept structural proxies, an appearance reference, and language through a shared interface. Training covers different proxy families, such as semantic layouts and shaded geometry, and multiple granularities within a family. Each checkpoint can follow fine constraints when supplied and synthesize plausible local motion when omitted, supporting different input granularities with the same weights.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">For video creation, users edit complete proxy sequences to refine camera paths, trajectories, and event timing. The bidirectional model attends across the full clip. During streaming, future states depend on actions yet to occur. The causal model therefore consumes proxy chunks and local text incrementally, generating each chunk in four steps using retained visual history.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.p5.1" class="ltx_p">We build on MiniMax-H3 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">42</a>]</cite> and adopt Guidance-Free Training (GFT) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">6</a>]</cite> to adapt its guidance-distilled backbone to proxy conditioning. Converting the resulting bidirectional model to a streaming renderer requires both fewer denoising steps and tolerance to errors in generated history. <span id="S1.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Progressive Forcing (ProForcing)</span> addresses these changes in stages (Figure <a href="#S4.F4" title="Figure 4 ‣ 4.3 Progressive Forcing for Few-Step Rendering ‣ 4 Invoker-Render ‣ Code World Model 2.0:Towards Infinite Controllable Video Generation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>). Teacher forcing (TF) first trains block-causal prediction on clean video prefixes. Resampling forcing (RF) then constructs imperfect histories by adding noise to observed prefixes and refining them sequentially with the current model.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p6" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.p6.1" class="ltx_p">RF-DMD retains these resampled histories while learning four-step generation through distribution matching distillation (DMD) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">64</a>, <a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">63</a>]</cite> and an auxiliary GAN loss <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib68" title="" class="ltx_ref">23</a>]</cite>. The student, trainable score model, and GAN discriminator then continue training on continuous self-generated histories in SF-DMD <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">18</a>, <a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">61</a>, <a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">14</a>]</cite>. Long-rollout training thus starts with a four-step generator and supervision models already trained alongside it.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p7" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.p7.1" class="ltx_p">We train on an aligned <math id="S1.p7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sim" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>∼</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sim</annotation></semantics></math>200-hour multi-granularity corpus with hierarchical text. Persistent history caching and pipelined proxy encoding and video decoding reduce serving overhead. Across 140 streaming rollouts, Invoker-Render outperforms recent streaming baselines in visual quality, structural adherence, and reference preservation, and maintains stable scene and subject appearance across 30-minute racing rollouts.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p8" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.p8.1" class="ltx_p">Our contributions are:</p>
<ul id="S1.I1" class="ltx_itemize" style="--ltx-enum-leftmargin:1.5em;">
<li id="S1.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Mixed-granularity proxy conditioning.</span> A shared conditioning interface lets each creation or streaming checkpoint accept coarse and fine proxies.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Progressive Forcing.</span> A curriculum progresses from TF/RF causal adaptation to four-step DMD with GAN supervision, then continues the trained student, score model, and discriminator under self-generated histories.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Long-horizon controllable generation.</span> Our four-step causal renderer outperforms recent streaming baselines and maintains scene and subject appearance across 30-minute racing rollouts.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.I1.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Multi-granularity corpus and serving stack.</span> An aligned <math id="S1.I1.i4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sim" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>∼</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sim</annotation></semantics></math>200-hour dataset and a low-latency distributed serving engine support multi-granularity training and continuous interactive streaming.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">2 </span>Related Work</h2>

<section id="S2.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">2.1 </span>Interactive Worlds and Generative Rendering</h3>

<div id="S2.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Action-conditioned video models often internalize world dynamics and visual synthesis in one network, learning latent or discrete action transitions from gameplay and video corpora <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">2</a>, <a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">52</a>, <a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">10</a>, <a href="#bib.bib17" title="" class="ltx_ref">4</a>, <a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">54</a>, <a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">57</a>, <a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">70</a>, <a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">40</a>]</cite>. LingBot-Video studies mixture-of-experts video pretraining for embodied intelligence, combining web videos with robot-oriented footage <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">39</a>]</cite>. Streaming architectures extend interactive horizons across open-world interactions and explicit context or 3D-aware memory, including the Matrix-Game series, WorldPlay, WorldCrafter, and related streaming world models <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib46" title="" class="ltx_ref">16</a>, <a href="#bib.bib47" title="" class="ltx_ref">53</a>, <a href="#bib.bib50" title="" class="ltx_ref">44</a>, <a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">68</a>, <a href="#bib.bib20" title="" class="ltx_ref">51</a>, <a href="#bib.bib51" title="" class="ltx_ref">66</a>, <a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">46</a>, <a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">13</a>, <a href="#bib.bib36" title="" class="ltx_ref">62</a>]</cite>. Because one visual transition model governs both state evolution and rendering, modifying scene structure or enforcing persistent physical rules remains challenging.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">A complementary paradigm maintains explicit state in an executable engine or agentic controller and delegates synthesis to a conditioned video model. Code World Model, Programmable World Model, and AgentGarten compile structured program state into visual signals <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">8</a>, <a href="#bib.bib28" title="" class="ltx_ref">20</a>, <a href="#bib.bib34" title="" class="ltx_ref">9</a>]</cite>, Marionette decouples state prediction, geometry rendering, and appearance painting <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib42" title="" class="ltx_ref">41</a>]</cite>, and Wizard supports real-time world manipulation via agentic control <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">55</a>]</cite>. StreamRender-H3, Streaming CWM, Magpie, and BoxWorld likewise couple game or simulator backends with neural renderers through semantic, white-box, or bounding-box streams <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib29" title="" class="ltx_ref">34</a>, <a href="#bib.bib30" title="" class="ltx_ref">28</a>, <a href="#bib.bib31" title="" class="ltx_ref">67</a>, <a href="#bib.bib37" title="" class="ltx_ref">56</a>]</cite>. Treating proxies as an explicit state-to-renderer contract, Invoker-Render studies controllable granularity across creation and streaming.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">2.2 </span>Proxy-Conditioned Video Generation</h3>

<div id="S2.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Building on spatial control, camera conditioning, and unified video creation frameworks <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib54" title="" class="ltx_ref">69</a>, <a href="#bib.bib57" title="" class="ltx_ref">15</a>, <a href="#bib.bib56" title="" class="ltx_ref">22</a>]</cite>, proxy-conditioned video models ground synthesis in geometric or semantic structure across several regimes. Paired methods learn directly from dense geometry, lighting, material buffers, or animated meshes, as in DiffusionRenderer, Generative World Renderer, and native 4D mesh rendering <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib55" title="" class="ltx_ref">26</a>, <a href="#bib.bib44" title="" class="ltx_ref">21</a>, <a href="#bib.bib45" title="" class="ltx_ref">7</a>]</cite>. Proxy2World relaxes paired supervision via posed RGB-D clips <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">59</a>]</cite>, whereas training-free methods such as Code Video Model restrict proxy injection to early denoising steps so appearance follows the reference image <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib26" title="" class="ltx_ref">27</a>]</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Recent renderers broaden representation diversity, customization, and structural fidelity. SolarRenderer reuses the backbone’s reference pathway across heterogeneous structural videos with a four-step acceleration LoRA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib39" title="" class="ltx_ref">12</a>]</cite>, EdenLive and Mundo support real-time reference-driven rendering and customized world synthesis <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib41" title="" class="ltx_ref">19</a>, <a href="#bib.bib35" title="" class="ltx_ref">36</a>]</cite>, Fight World Model controls combat interactions via visual proxies <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib38" title="" class="ltx_ref">25</a>]</cite>, and AnyGameRenderer preserves cross-game entity counts and timing <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib40" title="" class="ltx_ref">31</a>]</cite>. Invoker-Render targets an orthogonal axis: structural <em id="S2.SS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">granularity</em> within one representation family, enabling a single model to honor fine constraints when supplied and synthesize natural local motion under lightweight coarse proxies.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">2.3 </span>Streaming Video Diffusion and Few-Step Distillation</h3>

<div id="S2.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">While training-free queue scheduling such as FIFO-Diffusion enables continuous generation via diagonal denoising <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib59" title="" class="ltx_ref">24</a>]</cite>, interactive streaming requires block-causal attention and few-step sampling. Diffusion Forcing trains causal models with independent token noise levels <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">5</a>]</cite>, CausVid distills a bidirectional teacher into an autoregressive student <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib58" title="" class="ltx_ref">65</a>]</cite>, and Self Forcing rolls out the student on its own predictions <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">18</a>]</cite>. LongLive stabilizes rollouts via streaming tuning and a persistent frame sink <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">61</a>, <a href="#bib.bib69" title="" class="ltx_ref">58</a>]</cite>, SANA-WM and minWM scale minute-horizon and full-stack world modeling <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib48" title="" class="ltx_ref">77</a>, <a href="#bib.bib49" title="" class="ltx_ref">71</a>]</cite>, and AlayaRenderer-Flash and StreamRender-H3 co-design few-step causal rendering with low-latency serving <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib52" title="" class="ltx_ref">29</a>, <a href="#bib.bib29" title="" class="ltx_ref">34</a>]</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">To compress flow-matching trajectories <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib66" title="" class="ltx_ref">30</a>, <a href="#bib.bib67" title="" class="ltx_ref">32</a>]</cite>, consistency distillation maps states directly to clean targets <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib60" title="" class="ltx_ref">49</a>]</cite>, score-based distribution matching <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib73" title="" class="ltx_ref">35</a>, <a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">64</a>, <a href="#bib.bib75" title="" class="ltx_ref">75</a>]</cite> aligns distributions via auxiliary score differences, and DMD2, ADD, and LADD pair score or diffusion distillation with discriminator supervision <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">63</a>, <a href="#bib.bib74" title="" class="ltx_ref">48</a>, <a href="#bib.bib61" title="" class="ltx_ref">47</a>]</cite>. Multi-step variants refine supervision across steps, with Trajectory Distribution Matching (TDM) and VA-TDM aligning multi-step trajectories and velocity fields <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib76" title="" class="ltx_ref">37</a>, <a href="#bib.bib77" title="" class="ltx_ref">38</a>]</cite> and Endpoint Distribution Matching (eDMD) anchoring the fake score model on final clean outputs <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib78" title="" class="ltx_ref">73</a>]</cite>. For causal video, Causal Forcing uses an autoregressive ODE teacher, Causal Forcing++ and Causal-rCM adopt consistency-based causal initialization <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">78</a>, <a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">72</a>, <a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">74</a>]</cite>, and Salt++ aligns streaming generation and scoring contexts <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">14</a>]</cite>. ProForcing instead distills a four-step student with teacher-feature relativistic GAN supervision <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib68" title="" class="ltx_ref">23</a>, <a href="#bib.bib61" title="" class="ltx_ref">47</a>]</cite> on resampled data-anchored histories (RF-DMD) before continuing the coupled student, fake score model, discriminator, and optimizer states on continuous self-generated rollouts (SF-DMD).</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S3" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">3 </span>Data Curation and Proxy Construction</h2>

<div id="S3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Controllable rendering requires aligned training pairs that cleanly separate the geometry prescribed by a proxy from the appearance and local dynamics synthesized by the model. Our corpus comprises approximately 200 hours of footage, combining 150 hours of self-collected data with 50 hours from public datasets, and associates each usable RGB clip with structural conditions, an appearance reference, and hierarchical text annotations. We design the pipeline around three core requirements: spatial-temporal correspondence between proxies and RGB targets, multi-granularity structural representations of the same event, and language descriptions tailored to both whole-window creation and block-causal streaming.</p>
</div>
<section id="S3.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.1 </span>Data Sources and Coverage</h3>

<div id="S3.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#S3.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ 3.1 Data Sources and Coverage ‣ 3 Data Curation and Proxy Construction ‣ Code World Model 2.0:Towards Infinite Controllable Video Generation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> summarizes the corpus composition. Self-collected recordings allow us to render matched coarse and fine proxies from a shared reconstructed scene state, whereas public datasets broaden environment diversity and contribute native structural modalities. Reported durations count unique source footage prior to extracting overlapping training windows or multiple proxy variants. Figure <a href="#S3.F2" title="Figure 2 ‣ 3.1 Data Sources and Coverage ‣ 3 Data Curation and Proxy Construction ‣ Code World Model 2.0:Towards Infinite Controllable Video Generation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> illustrates representative source frames alongside their paired structural conditions.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<div id="S3.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_logical-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_middle" style="width:345.0pt;">

</figure>

<td id="S3.SS1.p2.p1.1.6.3" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_left ltx_align_top" style="padding-left:5.0pt;padding-right:5.0pt;">
