</span></td>
<td id="S3.SS1.p2.p1.1.7.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_border_bb ltx_border_t" style="padding-left:5.0pt;padding-right:5.0pt;"><math id="S3.SS1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sim" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>∼</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sim</annotation></semantics></math>200</td>
<td id="S3.SS1.p2.p1.1.7.3" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_bb ltx_border_t" style="padding-left:5.0pt;padding-right:5.0pt;">
<span id="S3.SS1.p2.p1.1.7.3.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:193.2pt;">
<span id="S3.SS1.p2.p1.1.7.3.1.1" class="ltx_p">150 hours of self-collected data and 50 hours from public sources</span>
</span></td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</div>
        
</div>
</div>
<figure id="S3.F2" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2611.22925v2/data_sources.png" id="S3.F2.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/336;" width="476" height="336" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 2: </span><span id="S3.F2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Source video frames and aligned structural conditions.</span> (a) Public datasets pair RGB frames with Magpie white-box geometry, CARLA depth, OmniWorld-Game depth, and Virtual KITTI 2 semantic layouts <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib31" title="" class="ltx_ref">67</a>, <a href="#bib.bib33" title="" class="ltx_ref">11</a>, <a href="#bib.bib32" title="" class="ltx_ref">76</a>, <a href="#bib.bib53" title="" class="ltx_ref">3</a>]</cite>. (b) Self-collected GTA V and Cyberpunk 2077 examples pair each RGB source frame with matched coarse and fine proxies of the same event, where coarse proxies place canonical root-driven bodies and fine proxies track articulated limbs.</figcaption>
</figure>
<section id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Self-collected data.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We capture gameplay across diverse 3D environments (including Grand Theft Auto V, Cyberpunk 2077, Elden Ring, and Forza Horizon 5), spanning navigation, urban driving, and character interactions under varied camera trajectories, weather, and illumination. Automated navigation and driving scripts yield sustained, smooth trajectories, while human gameplay contributes unscripted interactions and rapid viewpoint transitions. RGB frames and accessible engine buffers are recorded synchronously, with camera poses and dynamic object states recovered offline where engine exports are incomplete, preserving continuous multi-action trajectories for long-horizon training.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Public sources.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Public subsets contribute white-box geometry, semantic layouts, and dense depth, and Figure <a href="#S3.F2" title="Figure 2 ‣ 3.1 Data Sources and Coverage ‣ 3 Data Curation and Proxy Construction ‣ Code World Model 2.0:Towards Infinite Controllable Video Generation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> additionally includes Virtual KITTI 2 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib53" title="" class="ltx_ref">3</a>]</cite> to illustrate RGB paired with dense semantic segmentation. Source-specific preprocessing aligns native annotations to a unified frame rate and conditioning interface, applying geometric and temporal validity checks before enabling structural supervision. Clips lacking reliable structural alignment are retained solely for reference-and-text appearance supervision. Recording available condition types per sample allows public datasets to contribute their native modalities without requiring synthetic coarse/fine pairs for every source.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.2 </span>Aligned Scene States and Multi-Granularity Proxies</h3>

<div id="S3.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#S3.F3" title="Figure 3 ‣ 3.2 Aligned Scene States and Multi-Granularity Proxies ‣ 3 Data Curation and Proxy Construction ‣ Code World Model 2.0:Towards Infinite Controllable Video Generation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> outlines capture and proxy construction for our self-collected corpus. While recorded RGB serves as the supervision target, synchronized engine buffers and reconstructed 3D scene states (comprising camera intrinsics and extrinsics, static environment geometry, and tracked dynamic entities) allow us to render multiple structural granularities of the exact same visual event.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S3.F3" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2611.22925v2/data_pipeline.png" id="S3.F3.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/205;" width="476" height="205" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 3: </span><span id="S3.F3.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Capture and multi-granularity proxy construction pipeline.</span> Synchronized gameplay capture and 3D scene reconstruction yield aligned appearance targets, geometry, entity dynamics, metadata, and text annotations. From a shared scene state, the pipeline renders matched coarse and fine structural proxies for each event.</figcaption>
</figure>
<section id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Capture and reconstruction.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Starting from synchronized RGB and engine depth capture, our reconstruction pipeline recovers camera calibration, scene semantics, and 3D entity motion. Instance segmentation and multi-object tracking <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib63" title="" class="ltx_ref">45</a>]</cite> isolate moving actors and vehicles from the static scene, which is labeled via semantic segmentation and completed across invalid depth regions <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib62" title="" class="ltx_ref">60</a>]</cite>, while camera pose estimation and background point tracking recover globally consistent trajectories. For dynamic actors, human motion recovery estimates both global root trajectories and articulated body poses, and 3D bounding-box fitting tracks rigid vehicle motion. Retaining per-frame camera parameters, track IDs, and confidence masks alongside the video enables automated reprojection and tracking verification prior to proxy rendering.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Coarse structural control.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Coarse proxies encode global scene layout, camera motion, and entity placement and heading while omitting fine local geometry. Humans are rendered as canonical rigid mannequins driven solely by root pose, vehicles as oriented 3D boxes, and backgrounds as simplified geometry or semantic regions. Because a canonical mannequin conveys root translation and orientation without limb articulation, the paired RGB target and action text teach the generator to synthesize natural gait and posture consistent with the trajectory.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Fine geometric and motion control.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Fine proxies augment this representation with articulated human poses (rendered as depth-tested volumetric body parts) and shaded local surface geometry, while preserving rigid vehicle boxes. Wherever both variants are constructed, coarse and fine proxies share identical camera parameters, timestamps, entity identities, and RGB targets, directly supervising the renderer across constraint strengths for the same event. Throughout this work, we distinguish <em id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">granularity</em>, meaning the level of geometric and kinematic detail within a representation, from <em id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">representation family</em>, such as semantic maps, shaded depth, or white-box renders.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Separating structure from appearance.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To prevent appearance leakage, both granularities strip away surface textures, materials, and scene lighting. Before compositing dynamic entities, foreground masks are excised from background depth and semantic buffers and inpainted from temporally adjacent background views, suppressing silhouette cues from clothing, hair, or accessories. Reprojecting the simplified dynamic primitives onto this cleaned background with depth occlusion ensures that proxies convey pure spatial and motion structure, leaving appearance to the reference frame, language, and learned video prior.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.3 </span>Sequence Lengths and Hierarchical Language</h3>

<section id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Short windows and continuous sequences.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Self-collected and public recordings are standardized at 24 fps into 158-frame windows (<math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sim" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>∼</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sim</annotation></semantics></math>6.6 s) and 328-frame continuous sequences (<math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sim" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>∼</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sim</annotation></semantics></math>13.7 s). RGB targets use <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1344\times 768" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1344</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>768</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1344\times 768</annotation></semantics></math>, while aligned proxies are stored at <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="672\times 384" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>672</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>384</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">672\times 384</annotation></semantics></math> and encoded at <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="672\times 384" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>672</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>384</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">672\times 384</annotation></semantics></math> or <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="448\times 256" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>448</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>256</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">448\times 256</annotation></semantics></math> using nearest-neighbor resizing for semantic maps and anti-aliased filtering for continuous geometry. Short windows support bidirectional GFT, supervised TF/RF, and RF-DMD, whereas 328-frame sequences support variable-length SF-DMD rollouts across uninterrupted trajectories.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Whole-window descriptions.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Text annotations combine clip-level scene descriptions with timestamped local actions (“Scene + local actions” in Figure <a href="#S3.F3" title="Figure 3 ‣ 3.2 Aligned Scene States and Multi-Granularity Proxies ‣ 3 Data Curation and Proxy Construction ‣ Code World Model 2.0:Towards Infinite Controllable Video Generation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>). Each window pairs its opening RGB anchor with a vision-language caption covering environment, subject appearance, lighting, events, and camera motion. The bidirectional creation model and the bidirectional teacher and fake score models each receive independent whole-window captions rather than concatenated local tags.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Streaming action annotations.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Timestamped local annotations track action progression, motion directions, interactions, and camera shifts across block boundaries so that TF/RF and the distilled student observe text strictly up to the current block, without future labels or clip summaries. For coarse proxies, local text disambiguates behaviors whose articulation is omitted from rigid root geometry.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Condition organization.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">A system instruction defines the roles of structural proxies and the appearance reference alongside sample captions, while automated validation checks reference tags, temporal order, and entity-action agreement.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.4 </span>Quality Control and Evaluation Separation</h3>

<div id="S3.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Quality control screens both video and proxies for corrupted or frozen frames, exposure failures, shot cuts, reprojection outliers, tracking switches, and timing drift. Automated geometric checks and manual review evaluate each proxy against its intended constraints, distinguishing omitted coarse articulation from root-trajectory or camera errors.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Records track source identifiers, frame ranges, proxy variants, captions, and encoding provenance, with cross-source deduplication across shared game worlds. Training and held-out splits are partitioned by recording (and by scene or map where identifiable), keeping overlapping windows, coarse/fine pairs, and alternative views of one recording in the same split to prevent leakage.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">4 </span>Invoker-Render</h2>

<div id="S4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Invoker-Render adapts MiniMax-H3 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">42</a>]</cite> into both a bidirectional video creation model and a causal four-step streaming renderer. We first formalize the shared conditioning interface and linear flow parameterization, then present bidirectional proxy adaptation via Guidance-Free Training, and finally detail Progressive Forcing (ProForcing), which distills few-step causal rendering on data-anchored histories before transitioning to continuous self-generated rollouts.</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.1 </span>Rendering Formulation and Proxy Conditioning</h3>

<div id="S4.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{x}_{0}=(\bm{x}_{0}^{1},\ldots,\bm{x}_{0}^{B})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝒙</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>𝒙</mi><mn>0</mn><mn>1</mn></msubsup><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>𝒙</mi><mn>0</mn><mi>B</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{x}_{0}=(\bm{x}_{0}^{1},\ldots,\bm{x}_{0}^{B})</annotation></semantics></math> denote clean video latents partitioned into <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>B</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B</annotation></semantics></math> contiguous temporal blocks (corresponding to streaming chunks at inference time). Conditioning inputs consist of an independently encoded appearance anchor <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>a</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a</annotation></semantics></math>, structural proxies <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="p=p_{1:B}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>p</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>B</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=p_{1:B}</annotation></semantics></math>, a system instruction <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math>, and text annotations <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m6" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\ell=\ell_{1:B}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>B</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell=\ell_{1:B}</annotation></semantics></math>. Whereas the bidirectional creation model attends over the full proxy sequence <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m7" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="p_{1:B}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>B</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{1:B}</annotation></semantics></math> and a clip-level caption, the causal streaming model observes <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{b}=(a,s,p_{\leq b},\ell_{\leq b})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≤</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≤</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{b}=(a,s,p_{\leq b},\ell_{\leq b})</annotation></semantics></math> at block <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>b</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b</annotation></semantics></math> and factorizes the joint distribution autoregressively across blocks:</p>
<table id="S4.E1" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{\theta}(\bm{x}_{0}\mid a,p,s,\ell)=\prod_{b=1}^{B}p_{\theta}(\bm{x}_{0}^{b}\mid\bm{h}^{b},c_{b})," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝒙</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∏</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>B</mi></munderover><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>𝒙</mi><mn>0</mn><mi>b</mi></msubsup><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><msup><mi>𝒉</mi><mi>b</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>b</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{\theta}(\bm{x}_{0}\mid a,p,s,\ell)=\prod_{b=1}^{B}p_{\theta}(\bm{x}_{0}^{b}\mid\bm{h}^{b},c_{b}),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(1)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{h}^{b}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>𝒉</mi><mi>b</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{h}^{b}</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the retained visual history prior to block <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>b</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{\leq b}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≤</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{\leq b}</annotation></semantics></math> collects text annotations revealed through block <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>b</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b</annotation></semantics></math>. Target attention in the streaming model is bidirectional within each block and strictly causal across blocks. Both models preserve the Diffusion Transformer (DiT) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib64" title="" class="ltx_ref">43</a>]</cite> backbone’s native reference pathway and rotary positional embedding (RoPE) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib65" title="" class="ltx_ref">50</a>]</cite> indexing, keeping the appearance anchor <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>a</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a</annotation></semantics></math> fixed outside the training loss.</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Control across granularities.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Coarse and fine proxies enter through an identical conditioning pathway, trained jointly on mixed-granularity examples. Coarse inputs prescribe scene layout, camera trajectory, and entity root motion, while fine inputs further constrain limb articulation and local surface geometry. At inference time, downstream applications can select the structural detail suited to each interaction while relying on the appearance reference, text, and video prior to supply visual texture and unconstrained local motion.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Flow parameterization.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Given clean latents <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{x}_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝒙</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{x}_{0}</annotation></semantics></math>, Gaussian noise <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{\epsilon}\sim\mathcal{N}(\bm{0},\bm{I})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_mathvariant_bold-italic" mathvariant="bold-italic">ϵ</mi><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>𝟎</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑰</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{\epsilon}\sim\mathcal{N}(\bm{0},\bm{I})</annotation></semantics></math>, and noise level <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t\in(0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t\in(0,1]</annotation></semantics></math>, we adopt the linear flow-matching trajectory and velocity target <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib66" title="" class="ltx_ref">30</a>, <a href="#bib.bib67" title="" class="ltx_ref">32</a>]</cite></p>
<table id="S4.E2" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{x}_{t}=(1-t)\bm{x}_{0}+t\bm{\epsilon},\qquad\bm{v}=\bm{\epsilon}-\bm{x}_{0}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝒙</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝒙</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi class="ltx_mathvariant_bold-italic" mathvariant="bold-italic">ϵ</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><mi>𝒗</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_mathvariant_bold-italic" mathvariant="bold-italic">ϵ</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>𝒙</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{x}_{t}=(1-t)\bm{x}_{0}+t\bm{\epsilon},\qquad\bm{v}=\bm{\epsilon}-\bm{x}_{0}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(2)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">We write <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{v}_{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝒗</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{v}_{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math> for the velocity network and <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{f}_{\theta}=\bm{x}_{t}-t\bm{v}_{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝒇</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝒙</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝒗</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{f}_{\theta}=\bm{x}_{t}-t\bm{v}_{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math> for the induced clean-latent denoiser, omitting shared conditioning arguments where unambiguous. Here <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta^{-}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>θ</mi><mo>−</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta^{-}</annotation></semantics></math> indicates evaluation at current weights with gradients detached, and all squared-error objectives below are implicitly averaged over valid non-anchor latent elements.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.2 </span>Bidirectional Creation Model</h3>

<div id="S4.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Because MiniMax-H3 already incorporates distilled classifier-free guidance <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib70" title="" class="ltx_ref">17</a>]</cite>, we adapt it to structural proxy control using Guidance-Free Training (GFT) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">6</a>]</cite>. Pairing the full conditioning tuple <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c^{+}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>c</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c^{+}</annotation></semantics></math> with a weakened counterpart <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c^{-}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>c</mi><mo>−</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c^{-}</annotation></semantics></math> that drops the structural proxy while retaining the appearance anchor, we blend their velocity predictions at guidance scale <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta=2</annotation></semantics></math> with 10% condition dropout:</p>
<table id="S4.E3" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\begin{gathered}\widetilde{\bm{v}}_{\theta}=\frac{1}{\beta}\bm{v}_{\theta}(\bm{x}_{t},t\mid c^{+})+\left(1-\frac{1}{\beta}\right)\bm{v}_{\theta^{-}}(\bm{x}_{t},t\mid c^{-}),\\[3.0pt]
\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{GFT}}(\theta)=\mathbb{E}_{\bm{x}_{0},\bm{\epsilon},t}\!\left[w(t)\left\lVert\widetilde{\bm{v}}_{\theta}-\bm{v}\right\rVert_{2}^{2}\right].\end{gathered}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mtable displaystyle="true" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><mrow><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝒗</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>β</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝒗</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝒙</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><msup><mi>c</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>β</mi></mfrac></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝒗</mi><msup><mi>θ</mi><mo>−</mo></msup></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝒙</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><msup><mi>c</mi><mo>−</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mi>GFT</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mpadded style="width:0.497em;" width="0.497em"><mi>𝔼</mi></mpadded><mrow><msub><mi>𝒙</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi class="ltx_mathvariant_bold-italic" mathvariant="bold-italic">ϵ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>w</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo>‖</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝒗</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mi>𝒗</mi></mrow><mo>‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr></mtable><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\begin{gathered}\widetilde{\bm{v}}_{\theta}=\frac{1}{\beta}\bm{v}_{\theta}(\bm{x}_{t},t\mid c^{+})+\left(1-\frac{1}{\beta}\right)\bm{v}_{\theta^{-}}(\bm{x}_{t},t\mid c^{-}),\\[3.0pt]
\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{GFT}}(\theta)=\mathbb{E}_{\bm{x}_{0},\bm{\epsilon},t}\!\left[w(t)\left\lVert\widetilde{\bm{v}}_{\theta}-\bm{v}\right\rVert_{2}^{2}\right].\end{gathered}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(3)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Here <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w(t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>w</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w(t)</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the backbone’s time-dependent loss weighting. Detaching the weak-condition branch <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{v}_{\theta^{-}}(\bm{x}_{t},t\mid c^{-})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝒗</mi><msup><mi>θ</mi><mo>−</mo></msup></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝒙</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><msup><mi>c</mi><mo>−</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{v}_{\theta^{-}}(\bm{x}_{t},t\mid c^{-})</annotation></semantics></math> routes gradients exclusively through the proxy-conditioned pathway, sharpening structural adherence without inference-time CFG overhead. Trained under full bidirectional attention with complete proxy sequences and whole-window captions, the resulting checkpoint serves directly as our offline creation renderer and provides the initialization for causal adaptation and distillation critics.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.3 </span>Progressive Forcing for Few-Step Rendering</h3>

<div id="S4.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Directly distilling a bidirectional model into a few-step autoregressive renderer conflates trajectory compression with exposure to self-generated rollout errors. ProForcing disentangles these challenges across progressive stages (Figure <a href="#S4.F4" title="Figure 4 ‣ 4.3 Progressive Forcing for Few-Step Rendering ‣ 4 Invoker-Render ‣ Code World Model 2.0:Towards Infinite Controllable Video Generation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>). Supervised TF and RF first adapt attention to block-causal histories anchored to ground-truth video, RF-DMD then distills a four-step generator alongside learned score and adversarial critics under those data-anchored histories, and SF-DMD (Section <a href="#S4.SS4" title="4.4 Long-Sequence Self-Forcing ‣ 4 Invoker-Render ‣ Code World Model 2.0:Towards Infinite Controllable Video Generation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.4</span></a>) finally transitions the jointly trained system to continuous self-generated rollouts.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.F4" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2611.22925v2/proforcing_pipeline.svg" id="S4.F4.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/210;" width="476" height="210"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 4: </span><span id="S4.F4.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Comparison of ProForcing with representative causal video training recipes.</span>
Rows align five training pipelines across four functional stages from causal adaptation (Stage 1) to long-sequence tuning (Stage 4).
Self Forcing initializes from a bidirectional ODE teacher <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">18</a>]</cite>, Causal Forcing/++ and Causal-rCM initialize from causal teachers <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">78</a>, <a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">72</a>, <a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">74</a>]</cite>, and LongLive appends streaming long tuning <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">61</a>]</cite>.
ProForcing adapts block-causal attention via TF and RF (Stage 1), distills four-step RF-DMD with GAN supervision under data-anchored histories (Stage 2), and transfers the student, fake score model, discriminator, optimizer states, and student exponential moving average (EMA) directly into continuous long-rollout SF-DMD (Stages 3–4).</figcaption>
</figure>
<section id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Causal adaptation with TF and RF.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Replacing bidirectional target attention with block-causal attention, both Teacher Forcing (TF) and Resampling Forcing (RF) optimize the GFT objective of Eq. (<a href="#S4.E3" title="Equation 3 ‣ 4.2 Bidirectional Creation Model ‣ 4 Invoker-Render ‣ Code World Model 2.0:Towards Infinite Controllable Video Generation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>) under <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta=2</annotation></semantics></math> and 10% condition dropout. TF first conditions each block on clean ground-truth history <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{h}_{\mathrm{TF}}^{b}=\bm{x}_{0}^{&lt;b}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝒉</mi><mi>TF</mi><mi>b</mi></msubsup><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mi>𝒙</mi><mn>0</mn><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{h}_{\mathrm{TF}}^{b}=\bm{x}_{0}^{&lt;b}</annotation></semantics></math>. RF then bridges clean prefixes and imperfect inference context by corrupting each observed history block to noise level <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ρ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho</annotation></semantics></math> and refining it sequentially with the current detached model:</p>
<table id="S4.E4" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_table">
<tbody>
<tr id="S4.E4X" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S4.E4X.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\widetilde{\bm{x}}_{\rho}^{b}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝒙</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>ρ</mi><mi>b</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\widetilde{\bm{x}}_{\rho}^{b}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S4.E4X.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=(1-\rho)\bm{x}_{0}^{b}+\rho\bm{\epsilon}^{b}," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>ρ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>𝒙</mi><mn>0</mn><mi>b</mi></msubsup></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi class="ltx_mathvariant_bold-italic" mathvariant="bold-italic">ϵ</mi><mi>b</mi></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=(1-\rho)\bm{x}_{0}^{b}+\rho\bm{\epsilon}^{b},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="2" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equationgroup ltx_align_right">(4)</span></td></tr>
<tr id="S4.E4Xa" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S4.E4Xa.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\widetilde{\bm{x}}_{0}^{b}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝒙</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mn>0</mn><mi>b</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\widetilde{\bm{x}}_{0}^{b}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S4.E4Xa.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\bm{f}_{\theta^{-}}\!\left(\widetilde{\bm{x}}_{\rho}^{b},\rho\mid\widetilde{\bm{x}}_{0}^{&lt;b},c_{b}\right)." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>𝒇</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><msup><mi>θ</mi><mo>−</mo></msup></msub><mo>(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>𝒙</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>ρ</mi></msub><msup><mrow></mrow><mi>b</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>ρ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>𝒙</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><msub><mrow></mrow><mn>0</mn></msub><msup><mrow></mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>b</mi></msub><mo>)</mo><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\bm{f}_{\theta^{-}}\!\left(\widetilde{\bm{x}}_{\rho}^{b},\rho\mid\widetilde{\bm{x}}_{0}^{&lt;b},c_{b}\right).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.3" class="ltx_p">Conditioning each one-step refinement on previously refined blocks <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widetilde{\bm{x}}_{0}^{&lt;b}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝒙</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mn>0</mn><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widetilde{\bm{x}}_{0}^{&lt;b}</annotation></semantics></math> yields <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{h}_{\mathrm{RF}}^{b}=\widetilde{\bm{x}}_{0}^{&lt;b}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝒉</mi><mi>RF</mi><mi>b</mi></msubsup><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝒙</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mn>0</mn><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{h}_{\mathrm{RF}}^{b}=\widetilde{\bm{x}}_{0}^{&lt;b}</annotation></semantics></math>, exposing the model to realistic reconstruction errors while remaining anchored to observed trajectories. Throughout both TF and RF, history construction is detached, proxies and streaming text arrive block by block under the same <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta=2</annotation></semantics></math> GFT supervision and 10% dropout, and loss is computed across all target blocks.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">RF-conditioned distribution matching.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Initialized from the supervised RF checkpoint, RF-DMD compresses sampling to four steps via distribution matching distillation <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">64</a>, <a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">63</a>, <a href="#bib.bib76" title="" class="ltx_ref">37</a>, <a href="#bib.bib78" title="" class="ltx_ref">73</a>]</cite> while retaining detached RF history construction (<math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{h}_{\mathrm{RF}}^{b}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>𝒉</mi><mi>RF</mi><mi>b</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{h}_{\mathrm{RF}}^{b}</annotation></semantics></math>). Keeping histories anchored to observed video during distillation isolates four-step trajectory learning from open-loop autoregressive drift. To score student outputs, a frozen bidirectional teacher <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{f}_{\mathrm{teacher}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝒇</mi><mi>teacher</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{f}_{\mathrm{teacher}}</annotation></semantics></math> and a trainable bidirectional fake score model <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{f}_{\mathrm{fake}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝒇</mi><mi>fake</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{f}_{\mathrm{fake}}</annotation></semantics></math> (both initialized from the bidirectional GFT checkpoint) evaluate re-noised student predictions under complete scoring-window conditions, while the student itself remains strictly block-causal. Meanwhile, <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{f}_{\mathrm{fake}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝒇</mi><mi>fake</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{f}_{\mathrm{fake}}</annotation></semantics></math> is updated online via flow matching on detached, re-noised student samples.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Specifically, let <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{x}_{0}^{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>𝒙</mi><mn>0</mn><mi>θ</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{x}_{0}^{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math> denote the clean prediction tapped from a selected step of the student’s four-step denoising rollout, and let <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{x}_{t}=(1-t)\bm{x}_{0}^{\theta^{-}}+t\bm{\epsilon}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝒙</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>𝒙</mi><mn>0</mn><msup><mi>θ</mi><mo>−</mo></msup></msubsup></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi class="ltx_mathvariant_bold-italic" mathvariant="bold-italic">ϵ</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{x}_{t}=(1-t)\bm{x}_{0}^{\theta^{-}}+t\bm{\epsilon}</annotation></semantics></math> be its detached re-noised input shared by both score models. We apply the DMD gradient through the surrogate objective</p>
<table id="S4.E5" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{DMD}}(\theta)=\frac{1}{2}\,\mathbb{E}\!\left[\left\lVert\bm{x}_{0}^{\theta}-\bm{x}_{0}^{\theta^{-}}+\bm{g}\right\rVert_{2}^{2}\right]." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mi>DMD</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mpadded style="width:0.497em;" width="0.497em"><mi>𝔼</mi></mpadded><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo>‖</mo><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝒙</mi><mn>0</mn><mi>θ</mi></msubsup><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mi>𝒙</mi><mn>0</mn><msup><mi>θ</mi><mo>−</mo></msup></msubsup></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>𝒈</mi></mrow><mo>‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{DMD}}(\theta)=\frac{1}{2}\,\mathbb{E}\!\left[\left\lVert\bm{x}_{0}^{\theta}-\bm{x}_{0}^{\theta^{-}}+\bm{g}\right\rVert_{2}^{2}\right].</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(5)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p2.2" class="ltx_p">Writing <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{g}=(\bm{g}^{1},\ldots,\bm{g}^{B})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝒈</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>𝒈</mi><mn>1</mn></msup><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>𝒈</mi><mi>B</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{g}=(\bm{g}^{1},\ldots,\bm{g}^{B})</annotation></semantics></math>, the target-seeking displacement on block <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>b</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b</annotation></semantics></math> is <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{g}^{b}=(\bm{f}_{\mathrm{fake}}^{b}-\bm{f}_{\mathrm{teacher}}^{b})/Z_{b}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>𝒈</mi><mi>b</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝒇</mi><mi>fake</mi><mi>b</mi></msubsup><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mi>𝒇</mi><mi>teacher</mi><mi>b</mi></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>/</mo><msub><mi>Z</mi><mi>b</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{g}^{b}=(\bm{f}_{\mathrm{fake}}^{b}-\bm{f}_{\mathrm{teacher}}^{b})/Z_{b}</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Z_{b}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>Z</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Z_{b}</annotation></semantics></math> normalizes by the mean absolute discrepancy between detached student and teacher predictions (clamped to a positive floor). Treating <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝒈</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{g}</annotation></semantics></math> as a stop-gradient target ensures that differentiation of Eq. (<a href="#S4.E5" title="Equation 5 ‣ RF-conditioned distribution matching. ‣ 4.3 Progressive Forcing for Few-Step Rendering ‣ 4 Invoker-Render ‣ Code World Model 2.0:Towards Infinite Controllable Video Generation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>) propagates the exact normalized score difference into <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{x}_{0}^{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>𝒙</mi><mn>0</mn><mi>θ</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{x}_{0}^{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math> across all valid blocks.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Teacher-feature relativistic GAN.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">To sharpen perceptual detail and suppress few-step over-smoothing, we pair DMD with a discriminator <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{\phi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{\phi}</annotation></semantics></math> comprising frozen teacher backbone features <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib61" title="" class="ltx_ref">47</a>, <a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">63</a>]</cite> followed by lightweight trainable projections and a noise-conditioned scalar head. Ground-truth windows <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{x}_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝒙</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{x}_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> and generated windows <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{x}_{0}^{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>𝒙</mi><mn>0</mn><mi>θ</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{x}_{0}^{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math> are perturbed with identical <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(t,\bm{\epsilon})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi class="ltx_mathvariant_bold-italic" mathvariant="bold-italic">ϵ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(t,\bm{\epsilon})</annotation></semantics></math> via Eq. (<a href="#S4.E2" title="Equation 2 ‣ Flow parameterization. ‣ 4.1 Rendering Formulation and Proxy Conditioning ‣ 4 Invoker-Render ‣ Code World Model 2.0:Towards Infinite Controllable Video Generation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>) under matched conditions and the shared appearance anchor, producing scalar logits <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\phi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\phi}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{\phi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{\phi}</annotation></semantics></math>. We optimize paired relativistic logistic losses <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib68" title="" class="ltx_ref">23</a>, <a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">63</a>]</cite> alongside the combined student objective:</p>
<table id="S4.E6" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_table">
<tbody>
<tr id="S4.E6X" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">

<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S4.E6X.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\mathcal{L}_{D}(\phi)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mi>D</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ϕ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\mathcal{L}_{D}(\phi)</annotation></semantics></math></td>
