</table>
<p id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.3" class="ltx_p">Here <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda_{D}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>D</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{D}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda_{\mathrm{adv}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>adv</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{\mathrm{adv}}</annotation></semantics></math> weight the discriminator and adversarial terms, and <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\operatorname{sg}(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>sg</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\operatorname{sg}(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the stop-gradient operator on scalar logits. Discriminator updates detach generated latents <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{x}_{0}^{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>𝒙</mi><mn>0</mn><mi>θ</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{x}_{0}^{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math>, whereas student updates detach the real-branch logit <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\phi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\phi}</annotation></semantics></math> and freeze both teacher and discriminator parameters while backpropagating through the generated-branch input <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{\phi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{\phi}</annotation></semantics></math>. Note that <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{\phi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{\phi}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{f}_{\mathrm{fake}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝒇</mi><mi>fake</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{f}_{\mathrm{fake}}</annotation></semantics></math> remain separate networks trained under distinct objectives.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.4 </span>Long-Sequence Self-Forcing</h3>

<div id="S4.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Building on self-forcing and streaming long tuning <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">18</a>, <a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">61</a>]</cite>, SF-DMD replaces data-anchored RF prefixes with continuous student-generated histories. Starting from the appearance anchor <math id="S4.SS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>a</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a</annotation></semantics></math>, the student sequentially denoises each block in four steps and commits its detached terminal prediction <math id="S4.SS4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widehat{\bm{x}}_{0}^{b}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝒙</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mn>0</mn><mi>b</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widehat{\bm{x}}_{0}^{b}</annotation></semantics></math> to the causal history cache (<math id="S4.SS4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{h}_{\mathrm{SF}}^{b}=\widehat{\bm{x}}_{0}^{&lt;b}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝒉</mi><mi>SF</mi><mi>b</mi></msubsup><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝒙</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mn>0</mn><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{h}_{\mathrm{SF}}^{b}=\widehat{\bm{x}}_{0}^{&lt;b}</annotation></semantics></math>). While detached terminal outputs advance the rollout state, selected step predictions <math id="S4.SS4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{x}_{0}^{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>𝒙</mi><mn>0</mn><mi>θ</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{x}_{0}^{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math> retain local computation graphs for DMD and GAN supervision. Student weights remain fixed throughout the multi-block rollout, accumulate gradients across scored intervals, and take a single consolidated update before the next rollout refreshes its history from scratch.</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Local scoring of a continuous stream.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To supervise rollouts longer than the bidirectional teacher’s native window, we tile the continuous student stream with overlapping local scoring windows. Each window pairs preceding generated blocks (serving purely as detached temporal context) with a disjoint interval of newly generated target blocks, always retaining the original appearance anchor <math id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>a</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a</annotation></semantics></math>. The teacher, fake score model, and discriminator observe complete conditions within each local window while the student remains causal, and DMD and GAN input gradients are masked to apply strictly once per non-anchor target block, weighted by target coverage.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Coordinated continuation from RF-DMD.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Crucially, transitioning from RF-DMD to SF-DMD carries forward the entire coupled training state (student weights, fake score model <math id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{f}_{\mathrm{fake}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝒇</mi><mi>fake</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{f}_{\mathrm{fake}}</annotation></semantics></math>, discriminator <math id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{\phi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{\phi}</annotation></semantics></math>, their respective AdamW moments <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib71" title="" class="ltx_ref">33</a>]</cite>, and the student EMA) against the same frozen teacher. Because RF-DMD already converges a capable four-step causal generator together with calibrated supervision models tailored to its output distribution, SF-DMD avoids cold-start critic instability and focuses optimization on mitigating long-horizon error accumulation under self-generated histories.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">5 </span>Streaming Serving Infrastructure</h2>

<div id="S5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To deploy the causal world model as an online interactive rendering service, each streaming step must encode incoming visual proxies, update retained clean history <math id="S5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>H</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H</annotation></semantics></math> and current proxy conditioning <math id="S5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>C</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C</annotation></semantics></math> within a bounded KV window, run four-step causal denoising, and return decoded RGB frames within a strict latency budget.
Starting from a standard streaming baseline, we streamline the inference stack across three levels:
(i) an <span id="S5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">asymmetric streaming codec</span> pairing a lightweight Tiny AutoEncoder (TAE) for online proxy encoding with a causal video decoder for RGB reconstruction;
(ii) <span id="S5.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">intra-window invariant reuse and fused execution</span> across DiT layers, KV workspaces, and prefill/denoising passes; and
(iii) <span id="S5.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">cross-packet codec overlap and asynchronous CPU delivery</span> (Figure <a href="#S5.F5" title="Figure 5 ‣ 5 Streaming Serving Infrastructure ‣ Code World Model 2.0:Towards Infinite Controllable Video Generation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>).
On an eight-GPU node at <math id="S5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1344\times 768" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1344</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>768</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1344\times 768</annotation></semantics></math> resolution, these optimizations reduce the steady-state per-chunk period from <span id="S5.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">1770 ms to 930 ms</span> and increase throughput from <span id="S5.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">9.9 FPS to 18.0 FPS</span> (<span id="S5.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">1.82<math id="S5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math></span> speedup; Figure <a href="#S5.F6" title="Figure 6 ‣ 5.3 Cross-Packet Pipelining and RGB Delivery ‣ 5 Streaming Serving Infrastructure ‣ Code World Model 2.0:Towards Infinite Controllable Video Generation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.F5" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2611.22925v2/streaming_schedule.svg" id="S5.F5.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/276;" width="476" height="276"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 5: </span><span id="S5.F5.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Streaming inference schedule on an eight-GPU colocated pool.</span>
Each ordinary continuation chunk runs four DiT passes under Ulysses-8 context parallelism.
Pass 1 fuses deferred clean history <math id="S5.F5.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{n-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{n-1}</annotation></semantics></math>, the current proxy condition <math id="S5.F5.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{n}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_{n}</annotation></semantics></math>, and the first denoising step <math id="S5.F5.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{1}</annotation></semantics></math>; Passes 2–4 finish denoising, and only clean <math id="S5.F5.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H{+}C" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H{+}C</annotation></semantics></math> key/value states are committed.
During the codec interval between DiT windows, proxy encoding for chunk <math id="S5.F5.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n{+}1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n{+}1</annotation></semantics></math> overlaps with causal video decoding (<math id="S5.F5.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times 4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times 4</annotation></semantics></math>) for chunk <math id="S5.F5.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math>.</figcaption>
</figure>
<section id="S5.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.1 </span>Efficient Asymmetric Streaming Codec</h3>

<div id="S5.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Interactive streaming places asymmetric demands on the visual codec: incoming proxy frames must be encoded at every chunk with minimal latency, whereas generated latents must be decoded into temporally continuous RGB video.
Encoding online proxies with the full video encoder is slower than output decoding and dominates the inter-chunk codec interval.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We therefore adopt an asymmetric codec design.
The static reference frame is encoded once at session start with the full encoder to preserve anchor detail, while online proxy packets are encoded independently by a lightweight <span id="S5.SS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">TAE proxy encoder</span> directly into normalized <math id="S5.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="16\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>16</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">16\times</annotation></semantics></math> spatially compressed, 24-channel conditioning latents.
On the output side, we retain the tensor-parallel <span id="S5.SS1.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Causal Video Decoder</span> to preserve temporal continuity across chunks.
Replacing the online proxy encoder with TAE makes input encoding an order of magnitude faster than causal decoding (<math id="S5.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{\mathrm{enc}}\ll T_{\mathrm{dec}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>enc</mi></msub><mo>≪</mo><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>dec</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{\mathrm{enc}}\ll T_{\mathrm{dec}}</annotation></semantics></math>), reducing the steady-state chunk period from <span id="S5.SS1.p2.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">1770 ms to 1410 ms</span> and raising throughput from <span id="S5.SS1.p2.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">9.9 FPS to 12.4 FPS</span>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.2 </span>Intra-Window Reuse and Fused Execution</h3>

<div id="S5.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Within each DiT window, we eliminate redundant per-layer preparation, projection compute, memory allocation, and separate prefill launches:</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<ul id="S5.I1" class="ltx_itemize" style="--ltx-enum-leftmargin:1.5em;">
<li id="S5.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S5.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Cross-layer structural sharing.</span>
Within a single forward pass, all DiT layers share identical token layout plans, sliding-window crop indices, and frame-aligned RoPE position tensors.
We construct these plans and index tensors once at backbone entry and reuse them across all layers.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S5.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S5.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Per-layer AdaLN projection caching.</span>
Because session conditioning is stationary and the four-step Euler timestep schedule repeats across chunks, we cache each DiT block’s projected AdaLN modulation parameters by timestep and reuse them across subsequent chunks.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S5.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S5.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Transactional KV workspace reuse.</span>
Instead of allocating fresh output and concatenation buffers at every layer, we reuse pre-allocated KV result backplanes and temporary forward workspaces across the transaction lifecycle (Figure <a href="#S5.F5" title="Figure 5 ‣ 5 Streaming Serving Infrastructure ‣ Code World Model 2.0:Towards Infinite Controllable Video Generation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>, top).
Combining structural invariant and workspace reuse reduces the steady-state chunk period from <span id="S5.I1.i3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">1410 ms to 1180 ms</span> and lifts throughput from <span id="S5.I1.i3.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">12.4 FPS to 14.4 FPS</span>.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S5.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S5.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I1.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Fused prefill-and-denoise pass (<math id="S5.I1.i4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{H/C/D}_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_bold">H/C/D</mtext><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{H/C/D}_{1}</annotation></semantics></math>).</span>
In ordinary continuation windows, we defer committing prior clean history <math id="S5.I1.i4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{n-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{n-1}</annotation></semantics></math> and pack it with incoming proxy tokens <math id="S5.I1.i4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{n}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_{n}</annotation></semantics></math> and the first denoising state <math id="S5.I1.i4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> into a single block-causal composite forward (Pass 1 in Figure <a href="#S5.F5" title="Figure 5 ‣ 5 Streaming Serving Infrastructure ‣ Code World Model 2.0:Towards Infinite Controllable Video Generation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>), followed by three denoising-only passes (<math id="S5.I1.i4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S5.I1.i4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mn>4</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{4}</annotation></semantics></math>).
Reducing backbone launches from six to four trims the chunk period from <span id="S5.I1.i4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">1180 ms to 1165 ms</span> and raises throughput to <span id="S5.I1.i4.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">14.8 FPS</span>.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.3 </span>Cross-Packet Pipelining and RGB Delivery</h3>

<div id="S5.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">With intra-window DiT execution compressed, we pipeline codec execution and host frame delivery across packet boundaries to remove inter-chunk idle gaps:</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<ul id="S5.I2" class="ltx_itemize" style="--ltx-enum-leftmargin:1.5em;">
<li id="S5.I2.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S5.I2.i1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.I2.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I2.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Cross-packet codec overlap.</span>
Between consecutive DiT windows, causal video decoding for chunk <math id="S5.I2.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math> and TAE proxy encoding for chunk <math id="S5.I2.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n{+}1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n{+}1</annotation></semantics></math> run concurrently on disjoint GPU subsets (Figure <a href="#S5.F5" title="Figure 5 ‣ 5 Streaming Serving Infrastructure ‣ Code World Model 2.0:Towards Infinite Controllable Video Generation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>, center and bottom).
Because TAE encoding finishes well within the causal decoding window, next-packet proxy encoding is hidden behind current-packet decoding.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S5.I2.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S5.I2.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.I2.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I2.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Pipelined CPU delivery.</span>
Once causal decoding and the device-to-host copy into shared RGB memory complete, frame packing and socket emission are offloaded to an asynchronous CPU worker.
The GPU pool immediately starts chunk <math id="S5.I2.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n{+}1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n{+}1</annotation></semantics></math>’s DiT passes while host delivery proceeds in parallel, cutting the steady-state chunk period from <span id="S5.I2.i2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">1165 ms to 930 ms</span> and reaching <span id="S5.I2.i2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">18.0 FPS</span>.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS3.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<div id="S5.SS3.p3.1" class="ltx_logical-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_middle" style="width:345.0pt;">
          
<div id="S5.SS3.p3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<div id="S5.SS3.p3.p1.1" class="ltx_block ltx_minipage ltx_align_center ltx_align_middle" style="width:186.3pt;"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2611.22925v2/latency_ablation.svg" id="S5.SS3.p3.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:257/133;" width="257" height="133"></object>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS3.p3.p1.2" class="ltx_block ltx_minipage ltx_align_center ltx_align_middle" style="width:158.7pt;"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2611.22925v2/streaming_timeline.svg" id="S5.SS3.p3.g2" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:219/132;" width="219" height="132"></object>
</div>
</div>
          
<figure id="S5.F6" class="ltx_figure ltx_align_center">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 6: </span><span id="S5.F6.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Streaming inference performance.</span> (a) Cumulative per-chunk latency ablation showing the reduction in execution path and codec overhead. (b) Multi-chunk pipeline trace demonstrating concurrent codec and asynchronous delivery execution.</figcaption>
</figure>
        
</div>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S6" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">6 </span>Experiments</h2>

<div id="S6.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We evaluate Invoker-Render through systematic pairwise preference comparisons on causal streaming rollouts alongside qualitative studies of multi-granularity creation, camera control, and long-horizon streaming. Section <a href="#S6.SS1" title="6.1 Experimental Setup ‣ 6 Experiments ‣ Code World Model 2.0:Towards Infinite Controllable Video Generation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6.1</span></a> details the held-out benchmark and evaluation protocol, Section <a href="#S6.SS2" title="6.2 Quantitative Streaming Comparison ‣ 6 Experiments ‣ Code World Model 2.0:Towards Infinite Controllable Video Generation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6.2</span></a> compares our four-step causal renderer against representative streaming baselines, and Section <a href="#S6.SS3" title="6.3 Qualitative Results ‣ 6 Experiments ‣ Code World Model 2.0:Towards Infinite Controllable Video Generation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6.3</span></a> illustrates control across proxy families, structural granularities, camera paths, and extended rollouts.</p>
</div>
<section id="S6.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">6.1 </span>Experimental Setup</h3>

<section id="S6.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Benchmark and baselines.</h4>

<div id="S6.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We evaluate causal streaming rendering on a held-out benchmark of 140 test sequences spanning 6.58 s to 20 s across diverse 3D environments, multi-entity interactions, and proxy representation families, covering both single-window clips and multi-window streaming rollouts. We compare our ProForcing-trained <span id="S6.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Invoker-Render (Causal, 4-step)</span> checkpoint against three representative few-step causal and streaming proxy-conditioned renderers: <span id="S6.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">SolarRenderer (Causal, 4-step)</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib39" title="" class="ltx_ref">12</a>]</cite>, <span id="S6.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">StreamRender-H3 (2-step)</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib29" title="" class="ltx_ref">34</a>]</cite>, and <span id="S6.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Streaming CWM (4-step)</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib30" title="" class="ltx_ref">28</a>]</cite>. Every method receives the identical structural proxy video and appearance reference image on each test sequence.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS1.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Pairwise preference protocol and Elo metrics.</h4>

<div id="S6.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Effective streaming proxy rendering demands sharp per-frame synthesis, faithful spatial-temporal alignment to the driving proxy, and sustained reference fidelity across sliding windows. Following SolarRenderer <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib39" title="" class="ltx_ref">12</a>]</cite>, we use <span id="S6.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Gemini 3.8 Flash</span> to conduct blinded pairwise evaluations along four criteria. Each query presents the ground-truth structural proxy sequence, the appearance reference image, and two anonymized candidate renderings <math id="S6.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>A</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S6.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>B</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B</annotation></semantics></math> (uniformly sampled as timestamped frame sequences at <math id="S6.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="672\times 384" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>672</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>384</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">672\times 384</annotation></semantics></math> and 12 fps with randomized order balancing), eliciting an independent win, tie, or loss judgment along four axes:</p>
<ul id="S6.I1" class="ltx_itemize" style="--ltx-enum-leftmargin:1.5em;">
<li id="S6.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S6.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Visual Quality:</span> per-frame detail sharpness, suppression of synthesis artifacts, and temporal smoothness.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S6.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S6.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Structure &amp; Motion:</span> adherence of scene geometry, subject trajectories, action timing, and camera motion to the input proxy.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S6.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S6.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Reference Preservation:</span> stability of palette, illumination, material appearance, and subject identity relative to the reference frame.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S6.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S6.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.I1.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Overall Preference:</span> holistic quality as a coherent, deliverable rendered sequence.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
<p id="S6.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Pairwise preferences are summarized as <span id="S6.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Elo ratings</span> using the Bradley–Terry model <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib72" title="" class="ltx_ref">1</a>]</cite>, with ties counted as half a win and the mean rating across methods set to 1000. Overall Preference is evaluated independently of the three component criteria.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">6.2 </span>Quantitative Streaming Comparison</h3>

<div id="S6.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#S6.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ 6.2 Quantitative Streaming Comparison ‣ 6 Experiments ‣ Code World Model 2.0:Towards Infinite Controllable Video Generation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> reports Elo ratings across four criteria, and Figure <a href="#S6.F7" title="Figure 7 ‣ 6.2 Quantitative Streaming Comparison ‣ 6 Experiments ‣ Code World Model 2.0:Towards Infinite Controllable Video Generation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> shows Overall outcomes on 140 sequences per baseline. Invoker-Render ranks first on all four criteria, with an Overall rating of <span id="S6.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">1232.0</span>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<div id="S6.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_logical-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_middle" style="width:345.0pt;">

<figure id="S6.F7" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2611.22925v2/streaming_winrate.svg" id="S6.F7.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/124;" width="476" height="124"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 7: </span><span id="S6.F7.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Head-to-head overall preference against streaming baselines.</span> Bars show pairwise win, tie, and loss proportions of Invoker-Render (Causal, 4-step) across 140 blinded test comparisons per baseline, with the dashed vertical line serving as a 50% reference line.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S6.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Against Streaming CWM, Invoker-Render records 130 wins, 8 ties, and 2 losses, giving a 92.9% win rate and an Overall margin of <math id="S6.SS2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+539.6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>539.6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+539.6</annotation></semantics></math> Elo. Against StreamRender-H3, it records 116 wins, 4 ties, and 20 losses (82.9% wins and <math id="S6.SS2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+291.8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>291.8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+291.8</annotation></semantics></math> Overall Elo). Its margins over StreamRender-H3 are <math id="S6.SS2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+300.7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>300.7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+300.7</annotation></semantics></math> in Visual Quality, <math id="S6.SS2.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+197.6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>197.6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+197.6</annotation></semantics></math> in Structure &amp; Motion, and <math id="S6.SS2.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+281.6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>281.6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+281.6</annotation></semantics></math> in Reference Preservation.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS2.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS2.p4.1" class="ltx_p">SolarRenderer (Causal) is the strongest baseline across all four criteria. Invoker-Render leads by <math id="S6.SS2.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+61.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>61.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+61.5</annotation></semantics></math> in Visual Quality, <math id="S6.SS2.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+56.1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>56.1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+56.1</annotation></semantics></math> in Structure &amp; Motion, and <math id="S6.SS2.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+46.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>46.0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+46.0</annotation></semantics></math> in Reference Preservation. Its 88 wins, 2 ties, and 50 losses against SolarRenderer (62.9% wins vs. 35.7% losses) correspond to an Overall advantage of <math id="S6.SS2.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+96.7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>96.7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+96.7</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S6.SS2.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> Elo</span>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS2.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS2.p5.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#S6.F8" title="Figure 8 ‣ 6.2 Quantitative Streaming Comparison ‣ 6 Experiments ‣ Code World Model 2.0:Towards Infinite Controllable Video Generation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a> illustrates seven held-out sequences at matched late-rollout timestamps. Other works exhibit scene-geometry loss, severe texture artifacts, visible proxy geometry and flat proxy colors, or drift from the appearance reference at longer horizons: the underwater scene shifts into a bright sky, the winged character loses its wings, the deer loses its antlers, the red car turns beige, the road surface becomes blotchy, half of the ruined street turns black, and a narrow alley fades almost completely to black. Across all seven sequences, Invoker-Render preserves both structural alignment and reference identity.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S6.F8" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2611.22925v2/causal_comparison.png" id="S6.F8.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/220;" width="476" height="220" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 8: </span><span id="S6.F8.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Qualitative comparison of causal streaming renderers on held-out rollouts.</span> Each column shows one test sequence at a matched late-rollout timestamp (11 s to 18 s). The top shaded rows display the 0 s appearance reference and the synchronized input proxy, followed by frames from other works and Invoker-Render (outlined at bottom), which maintains both structural fidelity and reference appearance at the shown late-rollout timestamps.</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">6.3 </span>Qualitative Results</h3>

<div id="S6.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Figures <a href="#S6.F9" title="Figure 9 ‣ 6.3 Qualitative Results ‣ 6 Experiments ‣ Code World Model 2.0:Towards Infinite Controllable Video Generation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a>–<a href="#S6.F11" title="Figure 11 ‣ 6.3 Qualitative Results ‣ 6 Experiments ‣ Code World Model 2.0:Towards Infinite Controllable Video Generation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">11</span></a> further demonstrate how the bidirectional creation checkpoint and the causal four-step checkpoint operate across representations, granularities, camera trajectories, and rollout horizons:</p>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<div id="S6.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_logical-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_middle" style="width:345.0pt;">

</div>
          
<figure id="S6.F9" class="ltx_figure ltx_align_center">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 9: </span><span id="S6.F9.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Control across proxy representations and geometric detail.</span>
(a) Six examples spanning five proxy families, with synchronized input insets.
(b) Coarse, intermediate, and detailed geometry under a shared appearance reference.</figcaption>
</figure>
        
</div>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS3.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<div id="S6.SS3.p3.1" class="ltx_logical-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_middle" style="width:345.0pt;">
          
<div id="S6.SS3.p3.p1" class="ltx_para"><img src="2611.22925v2/camera_control.png" id="S6.SS3.p3.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/327;" width="476" height="327" alt="[Uncaptioned image]">
</div>
          
<figure id="S6.F10" class="ltx_figure ltx_align_center">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 10: </span><span id="S6.F10.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Two views of the same scene.</span>
Each row shows an opening view followed by two synchronized outputs from
different proxy-defined camera paths. Insets show the corresponding input proxies.</figcaption>
</figure>
        
</div>
</div>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
<figure id="S6.F11" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2611.22925v2/long_horizon.png" id="S6.F11.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:476/410;" width="476" height="410" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 11: </span><span id="S6.F11.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Long-horizon causal rendering on two racing sequences.</span>
Each case shows six matched timestamps, read from left to right. Rows contain the
input proxy, two prior works (A and B), and Invoker-Render. The upper and lower cases extend
to 298 s and 299 s, respectively, showing vehicle appearance and trajectory
adherence over approximately five minutes.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S6.SS3.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<ul id="S6.I2" class="ltx_itemize" style="--ltx-enum-leftmargin:1.5em;">
<li id="S6.I2.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S6.I2.i1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.I2.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.I2.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proxy families and geometric granularity (Figure <a href="#S6.F9" title="Figure 9 ‣ 6.3 Qualitative Results ‣ 6 Experiments ‣ Code World Model 2.0:Towards Infinite Controllable Video Generation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a>).</span> Across five structural families (semantic maps, sparse 3D boxes, subject masks, shaded geometry, and boxes with skeletons), the creation model adheres to prescribed layouts and actor motion while synthesizing coherent lighting and surface detail (Figure <a href="#S6.F9" title="Figure 9 ‣ 6.3 Qualitative Results ‣ 6 Experiments ‣ Code World Model 2.0:Towards Infinite Controllable Video Generation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a>a). Under a shared appearance reference, varying geometric granularity within one family (Figure <a href="#S6.F9" title="Figure 9 ‣ 6.3 Qualitative Results ‣ 6 Experiments ‣ Code World Model 2.0:Towards Infinite Controllable Video Generation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a>b) transitions smoothly from global layout guidance under coarse geometry to exact surface anchoring under detailed geometry.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S6.I2.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S6.I2.i2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.I2.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.I2.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Camera-path control (Figure <a href="#S6.F10" title="Figure 10 ‣ 6.3 Qualitative Results ‣ 6 Experiments ‣ Code World Model 2.0:Towards Infinite Controllable Video Generation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a>).</span> Each row pairs two views of the same scene and event at a matched timestamp, using a shared appearance reference and different proxy-defined camera routes. Coastal driving contrasts tunnel following with an overhead bypass. The rocket launch pairs ground tracking with an ascending drone, and the racing replay pairs a broadcast view with FPV following. These examples show how the supplied camera trajectory changes the viewpoint while retaining the scene and subject appearance.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S6.I2.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S6.I2.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.I2.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.I2.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Long-horizon causal streaming (Figure <a href="#S6.F11" title="Figure 11 ‣ 6.3 Qualitative Results ‣ 6 Experiments ‣ Code World Model 2.0:Towards Infinite Controllable Video Generation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">11</span></a>).</span> Two racing sequences are compared at six matched timestamps each, extending to 298 s and 299 s. Driven incrementally by incoming proxies, the four-step causal model preserves vehicle appearance and follows the prescribed trajectories across successive streaming windows. These examples complement longer 30-minute racing sessions with consistent scene and vehicle appearance.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S7" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">7 </span>Conclusion</h2>

<div id="S7.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We presented Invoker-Render, a proxy-conditioned video rendering framework that unifies bidirectional video creation and four-step causal streaming under a shared multi-granularity interface. Built on a <math id="S7.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sim" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>∼</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sim</annotation></semantics></math>200-hour multi-granularity video-proxy corpus, Progressive Forcing decouples causal adaptation and four-step DMD and GAN distillation on data-anchored histories from stateful continuation on self-generated rollouts, mitigating long-horizon drift while preserving structural fidelity and reference identity. Co-designing this renderer with a fused, KV-persistent, and codec-pipelined serving stack enables low-latency chunked execution, yielding consistent gains in visual quality, structural tracking, and reference preservation across streaming evaluations and sustaining coherent 30-minute racing rollouts toward infinite controllable generation.</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Several directions remain open for scaling proxy-conditioned world rendering. First, although our static prefix sink and sliding KV window bound inference cost and sustain appearance over extended sessions, visual details outside the active window are eventually evicted once they leave the local context. Incorporating explicit long-term memory mechanisms directly into causal training and distillation, such as learnable memory compression, spatial-temporal context retrieval, or persistent 3D-aware state caches, would allow the renderer to recall previously visited environments and maintain multi-entity appearance consistency across revisits. Second, because current training uses a fixed proxy granularity within each rollout window, supporting dynamic mid-stream level-of-detail transitions and coupling Invoker-Render with interactive state engines in closed loop remain promising avenues for future work.</p>
</div>
</section>

      should not be a barrier to accessing research. Thank you for your continued support in championing open access for
      all.</p>
    <p>Have a free development cycle? Help support accessibility at arXiv! Our collaborators at LaTeXML maintain a <a
        class="ltx_ref" href="https://github.com/brucemiller/LaTeXML/wiki/Porting-LaTeX-packages-for-LaTeXML"
        target="_blank">list of packages that need conversion</a>, and welcome <a class="ltx_ref"
        href="https://github.com/brucemiller/LaTeXML/issues" target="_blank">developer contributions</a>.</p>
  </div>
